## Contract review

Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/i18n-service.ts, packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/core/src/fallbacks/memory-i18n.ts, packages/services/service-i18n/src/file-i18n-adapter.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/objectql/src/formula-option-labels.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/option-label-table.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts

The remaining 14 files (tests, changeset, four `content/docs` pages) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head at review time: 14 completed `success` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter); 9 `skipped` (opt-in or queue-only jobs); 0 failed. STILL IN PROGRESS, no verdict yet: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI. This PASS is the design verdict; every type, test, generated-artifact and api-surface claim rests on those runs concluding green, and none of them was re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: `II18nService` gains optional `getSourceLocale(): string | undefined` and `setSourceLocale(locale: string): void`. RIGHT. Both optional, so no existing provider or consumer breaks; the shape copies the fallback pair, the precedent the card named.
- Accept-set: none moves. `TranslationConfigSchema.sourceLocale` keeps its `LocaleSchema.optional()` type; only its jsdoc and `.describe` text change (regenerated `references/system/translation.mdx` follows). RIGHT.
- Served answer: for a stack that declares `i18n.sourceLocale` different from `defaultLocale`, a request in the source locale now skips the fallback chain and a request in `defaultLocale` now walks it. RIGHT, and it is the card's ask. A stack with no `sourceLocale`, or with `sourceLocale` equal to `defaultLocale`, passes the same value as before at all five inline reads (traced: each reads `getSourceLocale` first and falls to the unchanged `getDefaultLocale` expression).
- `ResolveOptions.defaultLocale` keeps its name while its meaning widens to "authored language". RIGHT as a no-rename: the resolver code is untouched (prose only in `i18n-resolver.ts`), and the jsdoc says why the name stayed.
- Structural i18n slices in objectql (`engine.ts` twice, `engine-references-and-master-detail.ts`), plugin-email `OptionLabelI18n`, storage `UploadLinkLabelI18n` gain the optional getter. RIGHT: without them the engine's stored service type would hide the method from `readerOptionLabels`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `minor` on spec, core, runtime, service-i18n, rest, objectql, plugin-email, service-analytics, service-storage. Matches the diff: spec publishes two optional interface members (additive); core and service-i18n publish two new provider methods; the other six change a served answer only behind a newly honoured, optional declaration. No package in the diff is missing and none is listed without a source change. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Clause-②: yes` — correct; a published contract widens. PR body and changeset agree. The bare `yes` with no direction arm copies the claim line; the widening direction is what the diff shows.
- `Metadata-protocol: semantic` — correct; no key is added or narrowed, and what a declared `sourceLocale` makes the server answer changes. PR body and changeset agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question (inline read vs a shared helper): answered A, inline. Five 3-line reads in five packages with their own structural slices; a helper would be a further `@objectstack/spec/system` export for no behaviour. Accepted. The cost is visible in the tree and is a nit: four copies test `typeof source === 'string' and length > 0`, storage tests truthiness (`source || ...`). Equivalent for every string the contract allows.
- Deviation (surface beyond the claim): `rest-server.ts` (docblock only), `engine.ts` and `engine-references-and-master-detail.ts` (one optional type member each), three `content/docs` pages. Accepted: each is prose or a type the change would otherwise leave false, and none carries behaviour. `plugin-auth/**` is untouched, as the claim required.
- `serve.ts` and `dev-i18n.ts` left untouched: confirmed in the tree. Both construct `I18nServicePlugin` with `defaultLocale` / `fallbackLocale` only, and `AppPlugin.loadTranslations` reads `bundle.i18n` (else the manifest's) and calls the setters on whichever service is registered.
- Dev out-of-scope note 1 (`en-US` against `sourceLocale: 'en'` is not the authored locale, exact-tag compare): pre-existing in `isDefaultLocale`, unchanged. Not escalated; a follow-up card if the lane wants base-language matching.
- Dev out-of-scope note 2 (`ui/packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-formatters.ts` builds its chain from client config): outside this route and not measured by this review. Not escalated here; see N1 for the related server-side reader.
- Security: no `hits` path is under `skills/**`; nothing here teaches auth or permission behaviour. No `security` label owed.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Scenario traced on the head (`defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, `sourceLocale: 'en'`, no `fallbackLocale`, which `os serve` collapses to `zh-CN`): options become `{ locale, fallbackChain: ['zh-CN'], defaultLocale: 'en' }`. An `en` request is the authored one: own bundle, then the inline English label. A `zh-CN` request: the zh-CN row, then the chain, then inline. `ja-JP`: own bundle, zh-CN, inline, as before. A header-less request still falls to `getDefaultLocale()` in `extractLocale` (zh-CN), correctly not switched. No `sourceLocale`: `defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'`, unchanged.

Per `hits` file:
- `contracts/i18n-service.ts` — holds. The getter's "report, never invent" rule and the caller-side collapse are what all five readers implement. One half only: a provider with only the setter leaves callers on `getDefaultLocale` (the old answer, as the jsdoc says); one with only the getter works. `sourceLocale` equal to `defaultLocale` is a no-op. The `t()` sentence ("the value changes no `t()` lookup") is true in both in-repo providers: neither `t()` reads the new field.
- `system/i18n-resolver.ts` — holds. Prose only; `isDefaultLocale` and the chain builder are unchanged and already do what the new sentences say.
- `system/translation.zod.ts` — holds for the document translators. "A request in `defaultLocale` (when the two differ) walks the chain like any other translated locale" is true on the traced options. See N1 for the limit of the `.describe` sentence.

Census re-run on the head tree (every non-test reader of `getDefaultLocale` and every caller of the document translators under `packages/`):
- Authored-language readers that build resolver options: `metaTranslateOptions` (behind `RestServer.translateOptionsFor`, `form-routes.ts` twice, the list, single, view-container and plural-pair reads), objectql `readerOptionLabels`, plugin-email `servedOptionFields`, analytics `translateSelectOptions`, storage `labelsIn`. All five switched. No sixth builder exists.
- Users'-default readers, correctly NOT switched: `extractLocale` (rest), runtime `domains/i18n.ts`, discovery in `metadata-protocol` and `http-dispatcher`, service-messaging (recipient locale, notification text, push), plugin-auth email locale, the `I18nServicePlugin` log line.
- Translator callers that pass no authored language by design: `protocol-translated-echo.ts` (reads every locale to detect an echo; no chain, no default) and `lint-duplicate-field-labels.ts` (authoring tool).
- Coverage gate vs serving: `i18n-coverage.ts` reads `sourceLocale`, else `defaultLocale`; the five serving reads now use the same order. They agree on every document-translator surface.

Implementing files against the contract: `app-plugin.ts` (threads only a declared value, feature-detects the setter, placed beside the other two), `memory-i18n.ts` and `file-i18n-adapter.ts` (getter answers only what the setter was told, `undefined` otherwise, `t()` untouched), the five readers (source first, non-empty, else default; chain untouched), the objectql type slices — all agree, sentence by sentence.

Nits (no effect on this diff's correctness or the contract; none is to be fixed in code on this head):
- N1 (nit, follow-up card owed) — a class of label reader the census on the card and in the dev report does not list reads metadata labels through `t()`, not through `ResolveOptions`: objectql `resolveFieldLabel` (`validation/record-validator.ts`), `resolveOptionLabel` (`validation/rule-validator.ts`), `objectDisplayLabel` (`engine-validation-messages.ts`), and their users in `duplicate-record-error.ts` and `engine-delete-cascade.ts`. Read, not run: in the card's scenario `t('objects.X.fields.Y.label', 'en')` misses in `en`, falls to the collapsed fallback `zh-CN`, and returns the zh-CN row ahead of the declared English label — so an `en` write refusal still names the field in Chinese. This is pre-existing, outside the diff, and the same shape existed for `defaultLocale` after #15711; the contract deliberately keeps `t()` unchanged, and closing it needs a ruling (does `t()`-based label lookup learn the authored language, or do these readers move to the resolver). It does limit two new sentences: the `.describe` text "a request in this locale is answered from the inline text" and `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` "what the gate counts as covered is what gets served" hold for metadata reads, formula `label()`, email option holes, analytics and the upload-link page, not for validation and refusal messages. The seat should file the follow-up; the dev's HTTP boot covered `GET /meta` only.
- N2 (nit, accepted deviation) — the service holds one source locale per kernel and it can be set but never cleared. `defaultLocale` is required, so every `AppPlugin` resets it; `sourceLocale` is optional, so with several `AppPlugin`s on one kernel an app that declares none inherits a sibling's value, and its served answer can change although it declared nothing. Same property as the fallback pair, and the comment in `app-plugin.ts` states the guard is deliberate; the changeset's "a stack that declares no `sourceLocale` is served exactly as before" is exact for a single-app kernel only.
- N3 (nit) — `rest-server.ts` `translateOptionsFor` docblock: the edit now reads "All are feature-detected" beside the older parenthetical "both methods are optional ...; the core in-memory fallback declares neither", which was already inexact (the fallback declares `getDefaultLocale`) and now also omits that it declares `getSourceLocale`.
